## Imports

```{python}
import numpy as np
```


```{python}
def cal_score(score_matrix, seq1, seq2, i, j, match, mismatch, gap):
    '''
    Calculates score for position (i,j) in scoring matrix, also records move to traceback
    Args:
        matrix (numpy array): scoring matrix
        seq1 (str): sequence 1
        seq2 (str): sequence 2
        i (int): current row number
        j (int): current column number
        
    Returns:
        score in position (i,j)    
        move to trace back: 0-END, 1-DIAG, 2-UP, 3-LEFT
    '''
    if seq1[i - 1] == seq2[j - 1]:
        diag_score = score_matrix[i - 1, j - 1] + match
    else:
        diag_score = score_matrix[i - 1, j - 1] + mismatch
    up_score = score_matrix[i - 1, j] + gap
    left_score = score_matrix[i, j - 1] + gap
    
    score = max(0, diag_score, up_score, left_score) #Finds the max score, defaults to 0 if scores are negative
    
    
    #Determines direction based on score
    if score == 0:
        direction = 0
    elif score == diag_score:
        direction = 1
    elif score == up_score:
        direction = 2
    else:
        direction = 3
    
    return score, direction

```


```{python}
def traceback(seq1, seq2, traceback_matrix, maximum_position):
    '''
    Finds the optimal path through scoring marix
        
        diagonal: match/mismatch
        up: gap in seq1
        left: gap in seq2
        
    Args:
        seq1 (str) : First sequence being aligned
        seq2 (str) : Second sequence being aligned
        traceback_matrix (numpy array): traceback matrix
        maximum_position (tuple): starting position to trace back from
        
    Returns:
        aligned_seq1 (str): e.g. GTTGAC
        aligned_seq2 (str): e.g. GTT-AC
    '''
    aligned_seq1 = ''
    aligned_seq2 = ''
    i, j = maximum_position
    move = traceback_matrix[i][j]
    while move != 0:
        if move == 1:
            aligned_seq1 += seq1[i - 1]
            aligned_seq2 += seq2[j - 1]
            i -= 1
            j -= 1
        elif move == 2:
            aligned_seq1 += seq1[i - 1]
            aligned_seq2 += '-'
            i -= 1
        elif move == 3:
            aligned_seq1 += '-'
            aligned_seq2 += seq2[j - 1]
            j -= 1
        move = traceback_matrix[i][j]
        
    return aligned_seq1[::-1], aligned_seq2[::-1] #reverses the sequences so they are orientated correctly
```

```{python}
def smith_waterman(seq1, seq2, match=1, mismatch=-1, gap=-1):
    '''
    Smith-Waterman algorithm for local alignment
    
    Args:
        seq1 (str): input seq 1
        seq2 (str): input seq 2
        match: default = +1
        mismatch: default = -1
        gap: default = -1
    
    Returns:
        aligned_seq1 (str)
        aligned_seq2 (str)
        score_matrix (numpy array): scoring matrix
    '''
    column = len(seq1) + 1
    row = len(seq2) + 1
    
    #Initialize the matrix and fill them with int zeroes instead of the numpy floats
    score_matrix = np.zeros((column, row))
    score_matrix = score_matrix.astype(int)
    traceback_matrix = np.zeros((column, row))
    traceback_matrix = traceback_matrix.astype(int)
    max_score = 0
    
    for i in range(1, column):
        for j in range(1, row):
            score, direction = cal_score(score_matrix, seq1, seq2, i, j, match, mismatch, gap)
            score_matrix[i][j] = score
            traceback_matrix[i][j] = direction
            if score >= max_score:
                max_score = score
                maximum_position = (i, j)
    
    aligned_seq1, aligned_seq2 = traceback(seq1, seq2, traceback_matrix, maximum_position)

    
    return aligned_seq1, aligned_seq2, score_matrix
```

```{python, eval=FALSE}
# Example from slides
seq1 = 'TACTTAG'
seq2 = 'CACATTAA'

aligned_seq1, aligned_seq2, score_matrix = smith_waterman(seq1,seq2)

print (aligned_seq1)
print (aligned_seq2)
print (score_matrix)

```
